newsitem.title: UK: Clarke ahead in Conservative leader stakes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Clarke ahead in Conservative leader stakes - paper.

text.p: Britain's former finance minister Kenneth Clarke appears to be the front-runner in the defeated Conservative Party's leadership stakes, according to a newspaper survey.
But Clarke, the only noted pro-European among the six candidates, is ahead only because of a split in support for other contenders, The Observer survey suggested.

The Observer sampled the voting intentions of 82 of the 164 Conservative MPs entitled to vote in the election to replace John Major following the party's crushing defeat by Labour in the May 1 national election.

Of those, 21 said they were backing Clarke, followed by William Hague on 16 and Michael Howard and Peter Lilley neck-and-neck on 14 each, with John Redwood on 12. Stephen Dorrell was trailing with just five votes.
The leadership election is expected to take place within the next two months.
